title: State of AI Tokens 2026: Price, Volume and Return per Token
dek_2026: What a million AI tokens cost, how many tokens the largest platforms process, and what is earned and returned per token, 2024 to 2026 to date.

metrics.label: Tokens per $1 at GPT-4 (March 2023) quality, cheapest named model
metrics.unit: tokens per US dollar (3:1 input:output blend)

2024.source: DeepSeek API list price (DeepSeek-V3: $0.27 input / $1.10 output per 1M); Report AI calculation
2024.note: Blended price = (3 x input + output) / 4 = (3 x 0.27 + 1.10) / 4 = $0.4775 per 1M tokens; tokens per $1 = 1,000,000 / 0.4775. Bar: published MMLU at or above GPT-4's 86.4 (DeepSeek-V3 reports 88.5). A promotional price of $0.14 / $0.28 ran until 8 Feb 2025 and is not used. 2023 baseline: GPT-4 at launch (14 Mar 2023) listed $30 / $60, blended $37.50, = 26,667 tokens per $1.

2025.source: DeepSeek API list price (DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp: $0.28 input cache-miss / $0.42 output per 1M); Report AI calculation
2025.note: (3 x 0.28 + 0.42) / 4 = $0.315 per 1M. Smaller models that clear GPT-4 on some benchmarks but have no published MMLU above 86.4 (e.g. GPT-5 nano at $0.05 / $0.40, = 7.27M tokens per $1) are excluded, so this series is a conservative floor on tokens per dollar.

2026.source: OpenAI GPT-6 Luna ($0.10 / $0.50, after the 22 Sep 2026 cut) and Anthropic Claude Haiku 5.5 ($0.10 / $0.50 for prompts up to 100K tokens, 7 Oct 2026), as reported; Report AI calculation
2026.note: (3 x 0.10 + 0.50) / 4 = $0.20 per 1M. Prices are MEDIUM (secondary reporting; vendor pages not opened). Anthropic says Haiku 5.5's tokenizer uses about 30% more tokens for the same text, so tokens per dollar overstates text per dollar for that model. gpt-oss-120b listed at $0.09 / $0.45 on an aggregator in Aug 2026 (blended $0.18, 5.6M per $1; single source, not used). Change 2023 to 2026: 26,667 to 5,000,000 = about 188x; 2024 to 2026 = about 2.4x.

metrics.label: Usage-weighted market price per million tokens (Silicon Data LLM Token Expenditure Index, SDLLMTK)

2024.note: Index did not exist; no usage-weighted market price series for 2024 was found.

2025.source: Implied by a third-party explainer saying the index nearly doubled from about 1.09 to about 2.12 between December 2025 and May 2026
2025.note: Single secondary source; Silicon Data's launch value not seen. Treat as approximate.

2026.source: Axios, citing Silicon Data: index fell below $1, 54% under its late-May peak of $2.07
2026.note: 2.07 x (1 - 0.54) = 0.95 (same calculation as page 3441). 2026 readings found: 22 Apr frontier segment $4.20 and open-weight segment $0.85 (Silicon Data product page); peak ~$2.07 on about 28 May (Axios, Tokenpost; others give $2.12 or $2.05, CONTESTED); ~$1.62 in early July, about 20% under the peak (Bloomberg via secondary outlets); $1.16-1.18 on 6-8 Aug (SCMP); $0.97 on 31 Aug / 1 Sep (CNBC, Enterprise DNA); ~$1.00 on 21 Sep (Tokenpost). The 1 Sep reading was already below $1, so Axios's 'recent' break below $1 on 22 Oct implies a rebound in between or a lag (CONTESTED, as on page 3441). The index blends price changes with buyers switching models; it is not a list-price index and not a volume index.

2024: Google processed about 9.7 trillion tokens a month across its products in spring 2024, the baseline Sundar Pichai cited at Google I/O in May 2025.
Stanford HAI's AI Index 2025 found that the price of GPT-3.5-level inference fell from $20 per million tokens in November 2022 to $0.07 in October 2024, a decline of more than 280 times.
OpenAI's flagship GPT-4o listed at $2.50 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens from August 2024, about 229,000 tokens per dollar on a 3:1 blend (Report AI calculation).
ByteDance's Volcano Engine said its Doubao models were processing more than 4 trillion tokens a day in December 2024, 33 times the level at their May 2024 launch.
Menlo Ventures estimated that US enterprises spent $11.5 billion on generative AI in 2024, with spending on model APIs running at about $3.5 billion a year in November 2024.
2025: Google said in October 2025 that it was processing more than 1.3 quadrillion tokens a month across its products, up from 480 trillion in May 2025.
OpenAI said on 6 October 2025 that its API was processing more than 6 billion tokens a minute, up from about 300 million in 2023.

DeepSeek's September 2025 list price of $0.28 per million input tokens and $0.42 per million output tokens bought about 3.2 million tokens of GPT-4-level output per dollar on a 3:1 blend, against about 27,000 for GPT-4 in March 2023 (Report AI calculation).
Menlo Ventures estimated enterprise generative-AI spending at $37 billion in 2025, 3.2 times the 2024 figure; its November 2026 report restates 2025 as $33 billion.

MIT's Project NANDA reported in August 2025 that 95% of the enterprise generative-AI pilots it studied showed no measurable profit-and-loss impact, while Wharton's October 2025 survey found 74% of US enterprise leaders reporting positive ROI.
2026: Google said at I/O in May 2026 that it was processing more than 3.2 quadrillion tokens a month across its products, about seven times its level a year earlier.
Silicon Data's usage-weighted LLM Token Expenditure Index fell below $1 per million tokens by 22 October 2026, about 54% under its late-May peak of $2.07, according to Axios.
OpenRouter said it routed 790 trillion tokens in October 2026, 25 times its January volume, and that AI agents consumed 76% of them.
ByteDance said its Doubao models averaged more than 180 trillion tokens a day in June 2026, up from about 50 trillion in December 2025.
Menlo Ventures estimated enterprise AI deployment spending at an annualised $176.8 billion in September 2026, 5.4 times its restated 2025 total of $33 billion.

2024: 2024 was the year the price of a fixed level of AI capability fell fastest. Stanford HAI recorded GPT-3.5-level inference at $0.07 per million tokens in October 2024, against $20 two years earlier, and a16z put the general rate at about ten times cheaper per year. At the GPT-4 bar, DeepSeek-V3's December list price bought about 2.1 million tokens per dollar on a 3:1 blend, roughly 78 times what GPT-4 itself had bought in March 2023. The frontier moved differently. OpenAI's flagship GPT-4o bought about 229,000 tokens per dollar and Anthropic's Claude 3 Opus about 33,000: newer flagships were cheaper than GPT-4 had been, but the steep part of the curve sat below the frontier.

Volumes were still small by later standards. Google's 9.7 trillion tokens a month in spring 2024 is about 0.3% of the figure it would report two years later, and ByteDance's Doubao reached 4 trillion a day only in December. Microsoft's company-wide volume was about 20 trillion tokens a quarter early in the year, a figure we infer from its later statement that volume rose fivefold. OpenRouter, the developer routing service, handled on the order of 10 billion tokens a week in January 2024, on a single-source baseline. Most providers disclosed nothing, so any 2024 market total is guesswork and we do not publish one.

On the spend side, Menlo Ventures put enterprise generative-AI spending at $11.5 billion for 2024 and model-API spending at about $3.5 billion a year by November. Combined OpenAI and Anthropic run-rate revenue was roughly $6.5 billion in December. Evidence on return was thin: Wharton's survey implies about 65% of leaders reported a positive return, but no study tied that to what firms spent on tokens. Reasoning models arrived only in September, with OpenAI's o1, so the long chains of hidden tokens that would reshape task costs in 2025 barely register in 2024 data. In 2024 the question was whether to use the models at all, not what each token earned.
2025: In 2025 the price of a token stopped being the main story because the number of tokens per task grew so fast. Epoch AI measured the price of a fixed capability falling by a median of about 50 times a year, and DeepSeek's September price put GPT-4-level output at about 3.2 million tokens per dollar. But reasoning models multiplied the tokens behind each answer. Artificial Analysis spent about $2,767 running OpenAI's o1 through a seven-benchmark suite, against $109 for GPT-4o. On OpenRouter the average prompt grew from about 1,500 to 6,000 tokens. At flagship list prices, the average request cost about 2.2 times more in November 2025 than a year earlier, though the per-token price had fallen.

Disclosed volumes rose by one to two orders of magnitude. Google went from 480 trillion tokens a month in May to 1.3 quadrillion in October. OpenAI's API reached 6 billion tokens a minute, about 8.6 trillion a day. Doubao reached about 50 trillion a day in December, and China's National Data Administration put national use at about 100 trillion a day by year end. Taking only Google and ByteDance, the two that published comparable all-product figures, disclosed volume was about 2.8 quadrillion tokens a month late in the year, roughly twenty times the equivalent 2024 figure.

Spending rose much more slowly than volume. Menlo estimated enterprise generative-AI spending at $37 billion, later restated as $33 billion, and model-API spending at $8.4 billion by mid-year. OpenRouter's customers spent about $1.00 per million tokens routed. The return evidence split. MIT's NANDA study found 95% of pilots had no measurable P&L impact within about six months, and IBM found only 25% of AI initiatives met their expected ROI. Wharton found 74% of leaders reporting a positive return, and Snowflake reported $1.41 back per dollar. These studies asked different questions of different samples, so the results do not cancel out. They do show that the return was not settled.
2026: So far in 2026 the price picture has two speeds. At the GPT-4 bar, small models from OpenAI and Anthropic list at $0.10 input and $0.50 output, about 5 million tokens per dollar, 188 times GPT-4's 2023 price. The frontier has barely moved: OpenAI's flagship buys about 250,000 tokens per dollar after September's cut, close to GPT-4o in 2024, and Google has scheduled Gemini 4 Argon's price to double on 30 November. The usage-weighted market price, which did not exist before Silicon Data launched its index in December 2025, rose to about $2.07 in late May and then fell below $1 by October. Most of that fall came from buyers routing work to cheaper models, not from list-price cuts.

Volume growth has accelerated. Google reported 3.2 quadrillion tokens a month in May, and its API reached about 32 billion tokens a minute in the third quarter, more than four times a year earlier. Doubao averaged 180 trillion tokens a day in June. OpenRouter routed 790 trillion in October, 25 times January, with agents using 76% of them. Agents matter for the economics because they run loops of model calls without a person waiting, so tokens per task rise with autonomy. Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic did not publish 2026 token totals, which leaves the largest Western API businesses outside every volume series we can build.

Spending is rising, but more slowly than tokens. Menlo's annualised $176.8 billion for enterprise AI is about 15 times its 2024 base, and combined OpenAI and Anthropic run-rate revenue is near $115 billion. Google's token volume rose about 330 times over the same two years. On our calculation, spend per token is about 95% lower than in 2024. On OpenRouter, spend per million tokens fell from about $1.00 in mid-2025 to about $0.71 in August 2026. So the industry is selling far more tokens and earning less on each one. Jevons-style demand growth has so far outrun the price fall, which keeps revenue rising while margins per token narrow.

The buyer's return is still not known. Wharton's October survey has 80% of enterprise leaders reporting a positive return, but only 28% strongly positive. McKinsey has 37% reporting any EBIT contribution and about 6% attributing more than 5% of EBIT to AI, unchanged from 2025. One in five organisations told McKinsey that AI operating costs now limit their use. No company discloses return per token, and no published study measures it. What the data does show is that unit prices have collapsed, volumes have exploded and spending has followed volume only partly. Whether the extra tokens are producing proportionate value is a question these numbers cannot answer.

takeaways_2026: Two-speed prices: GPT-4-level output costs about $0.20 per million tokens on a 3:1 blend (5 million tokens per dollar), while OpenAI's flagship still costs about $4.00 (250,000 per dollar), close to its 2024 level.

The market price fell mainly through mix shift: Silicon Data's usage-weighted index dropped from about $2.07 in late May 2026 to below $1 by October as buyers routed work to cheaper and open-weight models.
Volume growth is accelerating: Google 3.2 quadrillion tokens a month (May 2026), Doubao 180 trillion a day (June 2026), OpenRouter 790 trillion in October 2026 with agents consuming 76%.

Spend follows volume only partly: on Report AI's index, enterprise spend rose about 15x from 2024 against about 330x for Google's token volume, so spend per token is about 95% lower; nobody discloses return per token.
yoy_takeaways: Tokens per dollar at GPT-4 quality rose from about 2.1 million (2024) to 3.2 million (2025) to 5.0 million (2026), against 27,000 for GPT-4 in March 2023, so most of the gain came before 2024. At OpenAI's flagship the figure barely moved: 229,000, then 291,000, then 250,000.

Google's monthly token volume went from 9.7 trillion (spring 2024) to 480 trillion (May 2025) to 3.2 quadrillion (May 2026); Doubao's daily volume went from 4 trillion (Dec 2024) to 50 trillion (Dec 2025) to 180 trillion (Jun 2026).

Enterprise generative-AI spend went from $11.5 billion (2024) to $37 billion (2025, restated $33 billion) to an annualised $176.8 billion (Sep 2026): about 15 times in two years, an order of magnitude less than token volume.

Reported business return improved only slightly. Wharton's positive-ROI share went from about 65% to 74% to 80%, McKinsey's EBIT-contribution share held near 37-39%, and the share reporting strong or full returns stayed below one in three.

faq_2026.q: How many tokens does $1 buy in 2026?
faq_2026.a: It depends on the model. At GPT-4 (March 2023) quality, OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna and Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 list at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens as of October 2026, about 5 million tokens per dollar on a 3:1 input:output blend. OpenAI's flagship GPT-6.1 Sol, at $2 and $10, buys about 250,000, and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, at $4 and $20, about 125,000 (Report AI calculations from list prices).

faq_2026.q: Are AI token prices still falling in 2026?
faq_2026.a: The average price paid is falling; frontier list prices mostly are not. Silicon Data's usage-weighted LLM Token Expenditure Index fell from about $2.07 per million tokens in late May 2026 to below $1 by 22 October 2026, according to Axios, largely because buyers switched to cheaper models. OpenAI cut GPT-6 Sol by 50% in September 2026, while Google scheduled Gemini 4 Argon's price to double to $4 and $20 on 30 November 2026.

faq_2026.q: How many tokens do AI platforms process?
faq_2026.a: Each platform uses its own unit. Google reported more than 3.2 quadrillion tokens a month across its products in May 2026, and its model APIs about 32 billion tokens a minute in Q3 2026. ByteDance reported more than 180 trillion tokens a day for its Doubao models in June 2026. OpenRouter routed 790 trillion tokens in October 2026. China's National Data Administration put national use at more than 140 trillion tokens a day in March 2026. OpenAI, Microsoft and Anthropic have not published 2026 totals.

faq_2026.q: If tokens are cheaper, why are AI bills rising?
faq_2026.a: Each task now uses many more tokens. On OpenRouter the average prompt grew from about 1,500 to 6,000 tokens between November 2024 and November 2025 (a16z / OpenRouter), and reasoning models and agents generate far more output. At OpenAI's flagship list prices, Report AI calculates that the average request cost about $0.0053 in November 2024 and $0.0115 in November 2025, more than double, even though the blended token price fell 21%.

faq_2026.q: What is the return per AI token?
faq_2026.a: No company or study publishes it. Report AI's proxies: customers spent about $0.71 per million tokens routed through OpenRouter in August 2026, down from about $1.00 in mid-2025 (derived from Sacra and Menlo Ventures figures), and enterprise spend per token is about 95% lower than in 2024 on our index. On the buyer side, Wharton's October 2026 survey found 80% of enterprise leaders reporting positive AI returns but only 28% strongly positive, and McKinsey's 2026 survey found 37% reporting any EBIT contribution.

stop_quoting.claim: AI inference costs have fallen 280-fold (cited as the current price of frontier AI)
stop_quoting.fact: The 280x figure is Stanford HAI's measurement for GPT-3.5-level capability between November 2022 and October 2024. At OpenAI's flagship list price, tokens per dollar went from about 229,000 in 2024 to about 250,000 in October 2026 (Report AI calculation).

stop_quoting.claim: The Silicon Data index shows demand for AI tokens is falling
stop_quoting.fact: The LLM Token Expenditure Index is a usage-weighted price per million tokens, not a volume or spend measure. It fell 54% from late May to October 2026 while OpenRouter's monthly volume rose 37% in October alone; Silicon Data itself has said the name misleads.

stop_quoting.claim: Google processes 1.3 quadrillion tokens a month
stop_quoting.fact: True for October 2025; Google reported more than 3.2 quadrillion a month at I/O in May 2026.

stop_quoting.claim: OpenRouter processes 10 quadrillion tokens a year
stop_quoting.fact: That is one week's volume (about 194 trillion, week of 26 October 2026) multiplied by 52, from a chart posted by an OpenRouter investor. OpenRouter's own recap reports 790 trillion tokens for October 2026.

stop_quoting.claim: 95% of companies get no return from AI
stop_quoting.fact: MIT NANDA's 2025 figure is 95% of generative-AI pilots with no measurable P&L impact within about six months. Wharton's 2026 survey has 80% of enterprise leaders reporting positive returns (28% strongly positive), and McKinsey has 37% reporting any EBIT contribution.

gaps: No figure is rated HIGH apart from the Anthropic list prices verified for page 421. WebFetch could not open any page (blog.google and ppc.land failed DNS in this environment), so company releases, Silicon Data's index page, Menlo's PDF and OpenRouter's recap were read only through search summaries.
Google has not published an all-products monthly token figure since May 2026; Q2 and Q3 2026 calls gave API tokens per minute only.

Microsoft has given no token total since fiscal 2025 (it now reports customers on track for 1 trillion tokens). OpenAI gave no API throughput at DevDay 2026; the '15B+ per minute' figure is unattributed. Anthropic does not disclose token volume (the S-1 coverage gives revenue mix only).
Not found: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio token volume, AWS Bedrock, Meta, xAI, Mistral, DeepSeek token totals.

Silicon Data's SDLLMTK has no published month-end series in the sources found; 2026 readings are irregular, the launch value (about $1.09) is implied by a blog, no November 2026 value was found, and the peak ($2.07 vs $2.12 vs $2.05) and the timing of the drop below $1 are CONTESTED.
No usage-weighted market price exists for 2024 or most of 2025, so the Jevons price index uses the GPT-4-bar list price instead, which is a quality-adjusted list price, not the average price paid.
Epoch AI's GPT-4-level price dataset could not be accessed; the GPT-4-bar series is built from named models' list prices with a published MMLU above 86.4 and is a conservative floor.
Menlo's 2026 report gives no dollar total for model-API spend; its 2024 base excludes inference and its 2026 figure is an annualised run rate, so the spend index mixes scopes.

Revenue per million tokens can be estimated only for OpenRouter (dependent on an assumed ~5% take rate) and roughly for Volcano Engine (whose token count includes internal use). No lab discloses both revenue and tokens served.

No published study gives token counts for the same task at 2024 and 2026 prices alongside a human wage cost. GDPval (Sep 2025) is the only cost comparison with experts found, and it excludes oversight and rework. No firm-level return per token is disclosed anywhere.
